# Dot & Dash Sensory

> High-contrast visual stimulation videos for babies 0-12 months, generated
> from a published, measured specification.

Independent producer of high-contrast baby sensory video. Unusually for the
category, the full production specification is published with measured values
rather than claims.

## Measured specification

- Contrast: 18.96:1 WCAG, 0.9937 Michelson (sRGB 10,10,10 on 250,250,250).
  Deliberately short of pure black/white for encoder headroom.
- Spatial frequency: repeating patterns run 0.08-0.35 cycles/degree across
  phone, tablet and TV viewing setups (74-97 pixels per degree).
- Motion: peak 797 px/s at 0-3 months, 959 at 3-6, 960 at 6-12. Median motion
  for most 0-3 month videos is zero.
- Flash safety: worst video in catalogue produces 0.56 qualifying luminance
  transitions per second, against the 3/second WCAG 2.3.1 threshold. That
  threshold is a general-population accessibility standard, not infant-specific;
  no infant-specific standard exists. Measured on a stricter 10% criterion than
  broadcast practice uses.
- Scene length: 8-40 musical bars at 48-116 BPM; 20-90 seconds per scene for
  newborn videos. No cross-fades.
- Palette by age: ink and paper only at 0-3 months; single red added at 3-6;
  yellow and blue added at 6-12.
- 39 videos, 1920x1080 at 30 fps, runtimes 4-45 minutes.

## Pages

- https://dotanddashsensory.com/methodology.html — full specification, the
  age-band table, viewing-distance arithmetic, and primary research sources.
- https://dotanddashsensory.com/how-to-tell-if-a-baby-sensory-video-is-well-made.html
  — five checks a parent can apply to any baby sensory video: contrast, shape
  size, motion speed, flashing, scene length.
- https://dotanddashsensory.com/are-flashing-baby-videos-safe.html — the
  three-flashes-per-second standard explained, who is at risk, what to watch
  for, and measured flash rates across this catalogue.
- https://dotanddashsensory.com/high-contrast-cards-or-videos.html — honest
  comparison; concludes cards are the better default under six months, and
  explains how to make them.
- https://dotanddashsensory.com/ — overview and parent questions.

## Position

Makes no developmental claims. States that paediatric guidance discourages
screen media under roughly 18-24 months, and that physical high-contrast
cards are a better fit than video for most families under six months.
